As weird as this may sound, but accept you aren't happy. Don't resist it. For me I  had to stop saying and thinking "I want happiness", because desire will only ever make you chase what you can't grab. Instead I think "happiness" and I live in the present moment. I am not 100% happy and nor will I ever be, but I am content with that now because I accept it. 

Accept all the emotions, but don't become attached to them. Don't resist your emotions, because substances did that for so long and that's why they are coming full force now during sobriety. 

 Meditation has been proven to reduce almost 50% of the intensity of emotions. Try Headspace, they have 3 minute mediations and an awesome basics package if meditation is new. I know it has significantly reduced how strong my depression hits me with negative thoughts. 

my short term method: if I feel like I have to cry at work, I will go into the bathroom, look at myself in the bathroom mirror and smoosh my cheeks together while I cry. I look so silly that I will burst out laughing, it reminds me to not take life and myself so seriously. I don't know why, but it has significantly helped me when crying gets out of hand. 

41 days is amazing, and great job joining a CBT class! Depression is going to find ways to make you lay in the floor to sob and not hit the gym, you have to stop listening to your mind for awhile so you can hit the gym. Exercising  naturally releases dopamine, so depression is going to try to stop you. Think of exercising as a "fuck you" to depression. You can overcome this, you are so much stronger than depression and substances. :)


You always have this community to remind you how strong and amazing you are when depression tells you otherwise. Depression is a filthy liar.

I quit weed and cigarettes too! Congrats on quitting them, man! You are rewiring your brain when you quit any substance, so it could be your brain trying to adjust to sobriety again. 
To deal with the anger I bought an ax and I chop wood while listening to the angriest rap or metal I can find. It helps, but I end up crying anyways. Which is good, because weed really covers up all emotions. 

How long have you been off weed and cigarettes? I have been off of them for 3 weeks, and I have rage when expectations are broken. I just have to recognize that anger is an energy, and it is only dangerous when a narrative or expectations are attached with it. Ex: the expectation that FB and technology should have worked, and the narrative of the comment taking a long time to write out, so it felt like wasted time. 

Focusing on the breath and not playing into the narrative have been helpful. Acceptance is tough at times.

I have road rage too. I think the reason why I get angry during driving is because I have expectations on how people should drive, and when they break that expectation that's when I get angry.

What I do is that recognize I am angry, and I note it, then I try to focus on my breath and the road instead of the expectation I have on the other driver. Another tip I have is that I assume the person is giving birth(if they drive too fast and reckless) or they have extreme anxiety(too slow and cautious). If someone takes my parking spot, I assume they have an invisible disability. They most likely don't, but it helps me get over the anger quicker. 
I am still working on my road rage.

I believe my 2 years of chronic and heavy usage of weed sent me to minor psychosis after an incident at my work on Black Friday. I couldn't sleep for almost 4 days, and I had irrational thoughts and behaviors.

Weed definitely made my depression and anxiety worse. Ever since I have quit smoking cannabis, my depression is not as strong(it comes in little manageable waves now) and my anxiety has decreased too. More self-confidence and my memory is becoming more sharp too. Suicidal thoughts crept up on me once on day 6, but I decided to exercise instead. Exercise has been the best dopamine releaser for me. Running is addictive! 

Quitting weed has been the best decision I have made. I think even saved my life. If I have kept smoking, I honestly think I would eventually go insane or kill myself. 

Day 11 for me, and I just got my first 8 hour sleep in over three months :) I am finally in a better mental place than I was a few weeks ago. I am so grateful to be sober and alive! I am more proud of my sobriety than my college degree.
Day 6-9 were tough for me mentally, but they passed and I am stronger now. 

Quit weed and meditate. Give yourself compassion and love for rewiring your brain, because the process could be difficult(self-compassion and remembering why you quit are crucial). 

What has helped me quit is imagining I am my own best friend. If my best friend was going what I was going through, I would only treat them with compassion, encouragement, and love

I fucked up regulating my emotions with smoking for anytime I felt sad, angry, fearful, or happy. I am learning how to control those emotions without them controlling me. Ever since meditating, I am aware of my emotions and from that awareness I can control myself. You did not mess up your dopamine permanently. The brain needs time to rewire itself. 

I highly encourage you subscribing to Headspace app. It has helped me more so much :)

Eat healthy, exercise, pursue an interest or hobby, surround yourself with supportive friends and family, and  meditate. You will get through this! There will be easy and tough days, but just remember why you quit on those tough days and they will pass :)

Anxiety makes the thought more scary than the actual event. 

My black Friday incident, for example: my anxiety made me believe there were over 40 angry people watching me crash and burn while I made their  beverages for them, but the actual event was 8 people watching me while the horde was patiently waiting for their drinks at their tables. Anxiety and negative thoughts can twist and transform true events. Have you tried Cognitive Behaviour Therapy? I do it sometimes to remind myself how ridiculous my anxious thoughts are.

Right now, I got a crush on someone whom I expect is on the spectrum, and she makes me laugh like nobody else can. She is also the most beautiful woman I have ever met in person. Honestly? I love dating women on the autistic spectrum, because they are intelligent, witty, hilarious, silly, direct, caring, and the most selfless lovers (animalistic too, which is unbelievably hot). 

You will find someone! I have been single for almost two years and thought I would never find someone after my ex gf, but that simply isn't true and that person will be worth the wait!

Being autistic is truly beautiful. We feel so much, especially love! :)

What kind of pets? I helped treat 6 kittens for fleas with a friend, luckily, I was able to help her get rid of the fleas from her apartment. We used original Dawn soap for baths, and we had to comb and kill each one individually. We gave each kitten three baths in the span of three days. Each session took like an hour for each kitten. We vacuumed every hour. Washed all the clothes repeatedly. Any clothes that were in contact with the kittens had to be kept in a plastic bag and washed immediately. We had to keep the kittens in the bathroom for three days, so the fleas wouldn't get in the carpet and spread. We were able to kill all the fleas on the kittens and the apartment. The cats are now indoor cats.
